Hey milkeyway,

I'm certainly no standard to follow, but I took this homework as two-fold: 1. why did the decision occur?; 2. how did the decision occur? #1 speaks to the history of a given price. #2 is what's happening as price turns. If you're interested in an illustration, you can see my post from earlier this week. I tried to find out what supply, demand, FL, etc. in history made price turn where it did (#1), and also how price turned when it did (#2) - was it a QM, ENG, FO, etc.?

it's what I focused on. Hope that helps in your homework!

fxyogi wrote: Can somebody help me to tell the difference between FTR and FL?

RBR/DBD= FL = DECISION. FTR= Price fails to return after breaking the low or high.

The important thing is thinking about the FL and FTR which are significant. Watch IF's AU season video. Whenever I lost my hope, I watch the video.

Dear FXyogi....i have had more than a few failed trades lately...and started to question myself...then i remembered o quote i have read somewhere that said something like "When you experience failure, it is really success letting you know that you have identified a flaw that needs to be corrected or removed" so i started to analyze every failed trade and drawn the conclusion that i'm not one with the market yet but most important that my targets were too optimistic.Every failed trade i had was in profit until the first trouble area...where of course it didn't engulf and continued in the original direction....I suggest you to do the same with your trades.

First of all it is my thinking that RTM doesn't teach us a method but gives us the decryption keys of what once seemed an encrypted chaos.It is up to us to develop a method based on what we learn....and of course develop the all needed discipline.Think of this if you only searched for your very very best 1:3 setups and took them...with only 200 trades with 2% risk you add 5 zeros to your account.(thats 100.000.000 from 1000).I'm not saying you will not have losses but what's the point of taking lame and shady trades if you can wait for the very best setups (like Harry said"i don't go on blind dates in dark alleys " )..I'm writing this to encourage you to proceed on your journey I know that watching IF's charts and trades and other members it may give you the confidence that RTM setups are fail safe...BUT they are safe untill the next decision point...further it's just a gamble if we don't get PA(engulf).And they have spent maybe 10000 s of hours before they trade like that. You need to lose the mentality of trading systems preached everywhere on the net...you can't have rules...more like guidelines.....price is a story with a plot that builds and changes constantly upon earlier events.....all we can do is use what we learned here (FL,FTR,Engulf,Fo) and if all the holes line up in the swiss cheese then we take the trade...but using the appropriate risk apetite.And if the story is unclear stay out....a good trader isn't the sum of all the trades he takes....but how he adapts to the environment he's in without "bleeding" too much.

Maybe you should treat this as a hobby at first so that you don't feel the pressure to succeed.Allocate a few hours daily or weekly to learn.Take every master elite and associate trader posts from the beginning on this forum and read them...save the charts and save their words of wisdom.I write them with pen and paper...i think they sink in better this way.And when you have finished take all your quotes and organize them into the categories found in Marketpedia.And then start in the homework....Now this is one of the highly profitable business on earth...do you think it can be done without some sort of leap of faith?or sweat?...

But you need to set your priorities straight.

Namaste
